notes: Enemies follow one fixed route to a core while the player buys and places towers along it, so this is Strategy's Tower Defense on lane-actor-track, and its P6 holds because the route has to be a single valid continuous path for the waves and for the path-progress damage model the spec is built on. Action is named second because the engineer is physically in the arena dodging their own towers' fire and swinging a wrench, which is why this is emphatically not a SET the way an overhead tower defense would be — the player walks the same ground the projectiles cross. cover-los is a real pick rather than preset filler: the spec has world geometry that destroys projectiles and tagged blockers, and Strategy's wording of it, keeping any one placement from dominating, is the one that applies since Strategy leads. I kept the choke point for the bends the pulse tower is described as excelling at, and took the author's compact stylized foundry — metal platforms, pipes, furnaces, molten lighting — as dressing on a single planar 120-stud arena; the scrap pickups spawn at enemy death positions at runtime, so there is no fixed collectible site to place, and the Luau architecture rules are implementation rather than layout.
